rules.title: California fair housing law: source-of-income and subsidy-based income standards in tenant screening
rules.requirement: Where a government rent subsidy applies, a housing provider may not use an income standard that is not based on the portion of rent the tenant pays. A provider that uses credit history must let the applicant choose to offer alternative evidence of ability to pay, give reasonable time to respond, and reasonably consider that evidence instead of credit history. Income standards must count the aggregate income of persons residing together on the same basis as married persons. 'Source of income' covers lawful, verifiable income, including public assistance and housing subsidies such as Section 8 and HUD-VASH vouchers. Landlords may still verify employment, request references and verify identity.

coverage.summary: Applies to housing providers renting housing in California; no unit-count or construction-date limits are stated in the passages.

rules.effective_date_note: The passages do not state an effective date.
rules.quoted_span: (A) Use a financial or income standard in assessing eligibility for the rental of housing that is not based on the portion of the rent to be paid by the tenant.
rules.review_note: The passage excerpts do not print the section number. The Gov. Code § 12955 citation is inferred from the subdivision structure and should be verified.
rules.source_notes: The CRD FAQ (D016) confirms that refusing to rent based on source of income, including Section 8 vouchers, is prohibited.

rules.title: California Civil Rights Council regulations on criminal history in housing decisions
rules.requirement: Housing providers may check criminal history but may not consider arrests that did not lead to conviction, sealed or expunged records, or juvenile justice records. Blanket bans on applicants with a criminal record are prohibited. A denial based on a conviction must be directly related to the applicant's ability to be a good tenant and to not threaten the health and safety of others or the property. Providers should weigh the nature and severity of the offense and the time elapsed since it.

coverage.summary: Applies to housing providers in California; no unit-count or construction-date limits are stated in the passages.

rules.effective_date_note: The effective date comes from a secondary source (CAA), which says the regulations 'took effect Jan. 1, 2020'.
